name: The Democrat's printers
head: pratt_oscar

arrival.note: They are in Calhoun's employ in the autumn of 1833, so they were in the town by then. Nothing dates their coming and nothing says they came with him.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

reason_for_coming.value: Employment at the town's first printing office
reason_for_coming.note: They are named as employees of the man who founded the paper. The inference is that the work is why they were here.

lives_at.note: Not attested. Journeymen printers of this period often boarded and often slept in the office; neither is claimed here.

works_at.note: 'In the employ of Mr. Calhoun', whose office's address the paper itself prints.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1673/1857`, which reaches 1857-12-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: They are documented in the office in the autumn of 1833 and nothing follows them to 1835. Journeyman printers were the most mobile trade in a frontier town. Recorded as uncertain rather than assumed forward.

persons.name: Oscar Pratt

occupation.note: Andreas's 1833 roster: 'Oscar Pratt and Beckford, printers, were in the employ of Mr. Calhoun at that time.'

persons.note: A REAL, NAMED MAN WITH A TRADE AND AN EMPLOYER, and nothing else. Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named' - a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, compiled fifty years after the fact.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 20 under 30', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('pratt_oscar:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

The sex field is omitted rather than assumed: a compositor in 1833 was overwhelmingly likely to be a man, but 'overwhelmingly likely' is not what documented means and this record has no other information about the person at all.

research_note: TWO WAGE-EARNERS, WHICH THIS DATASET OTHERWISE HAS ALMOST NONE OF, and a household that is a household only by convention. Andreas names them in one clause, as a pair, in an employment; nothing states where either lived or whether they lived together, and the grouping is a container for two people the source presents together, not a claim about a dwelling. lives_at is null for that reason and must stay null. WHY THEY ARE WORTH WRITING: the documented population of early Chicago as the sources give it is overwhelmingly proprietors - the men who owned the store, kept the tavern, edited the paper. The people who did the work are named perhaps a dozen times in the whole of Andreas's first volume, and these two are among them. The inferred phase's largest single task is the rest of them.
